summary: Command-line tool that packs a whole code repository into one AI-friendly file you can paste into Claude, ChatGPT or other LLMs.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Repomix bundles all the files in a repository into a single file (repomix-output.xml by default) laid out so an AI model can read the whole codebase at once. It counts tokens per file and in total, respects .gitignore, can compress code to its key structure with Tree-sitter, and checks for secrets before you share.
sixtySeconds.problem: Giving an LLM your codebase file by file is slow and loses context. Repomix makes one file you can attach with a prompt like 'review this before I refactor'.
whoFor: Developers who chat with AI about their code
People reviewing or documenting repositories with AI
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a one-command pack with token counts, ignore-file support, compression and Secretlint-based secret detection.
requirements: Or Homebrew, or the browser version at repomix.com

overview: Run npx repomix@latest in your project folder to try it without installing, or install it globally with npm, yarn, bun or Homebrew and run repomix.
It writes repomix-output.xml in the current folder. You can pack a sub-folder, include or exclude glob patterns, pack a remote GitHub repo with --remote, and shrink output with --compress.
There are also browser extensions, a website at repomix.com, a GitHub Action and a library API. It is MIT licensed.
limitations: Large repos can still exceed model limits
Output is a snapshot, not live
